2027-03-25.title: Pesaha · The Lord's Supper
readings: Let anyone who is thirsty come to me
Do not walk with those who lie in wait for blood
The Lord will reign on Mount Zion
The marriage supper of the Lamb
Do this in remembrance of me
2027-03-25.alt: Pesaha (Maundy Thursday). In 2027 the date of the Annunciation (25 March) falls on this day; follow the direction of your eparchy on how the Annunciation is kept.
2027-03-25.verse: Then he took a loaf of bread, and when he had given thanks, he broke it and gave it to them, saying, “This is my body, which is given for you. Do this in remembrance of me.”
theo: On the night before he suffered, Jesus gathered his apostles in the upper room. “I have eagerly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.” At that table he took bread, gave thanks, broke it and said: “This is my body, which is given for you. Do this in remembrance of me.” And after supper he took the cup: “This cup that is poured out for you is the new covenant in my blood.” On this night the Holy Qurbono was born.

Exodus tells of the first Passover: a lamb without blemish, its blood on the doorposts, eaten in haste by a people ready to leave slavery. “When I see the blood, I will pass over you.” Jesus is the true Passover Lamb. His blood marks us, his Body feeds us for the journey from slavery to freedom, from death to life.

At the same table Jesus gave his apostles a lesson in greatness: “Who is greater, the one who is at the table or the one who serves? Is it not the one at the table? But I am among you as one who serves.” In our tradition the washing of feet makes this visible. The Eucharist and service cannot be separated: the One who gives his Body washes our feet.

St Paul hands on what he received: “For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until he comes.” He also warns against receiving unworthily. Pesaha is the night to thank God for the Holy Qurbono and the priesthood, to examine our hearts, and to stay awake with Jesus as he goes out to Gethsemane.
conn: Exodus 12: the unblemished lamb whose blood saves; John 1:29 and 1 Corinthians 5:7: “Christ, our paschal lamb, has been sacrificed.”
Leviticus 16: the high priest enters the Holy of Holies with blood; Christ is priest and victim (Hebrews 9:11–14).
John 7:37–38: from the heart of Christ flow streams of living water, fulfilled when his side is pierced (John 19:34).
The wedding supper of the Lamb.
Revelation 19:9: “Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb”: every Qurbono is a foretaste.
altar: Tonight we celebrate the Holy Qurbono at the very hour of its institution. The words the priest says over the bread and wine are the words of the upper room. Thank God tonight for every Qurbono you have received, and for the priests who celebrate it.
outline: The upper room: “I have eagerly desired to eat this Passover with you.”
From the lamb of Egypt to the Lamb of God.
The real presence: Christ gives himself.
The washing of feet: Eucharist and service.
Gethsemane: watch and pray with Jesus tonight.
live: Share the Pesaha appam and paal as a family, praying for unity and remembering the Last Supper.
Spend time in adoration tonight, keeping Jesus company.
Do one humble service for a family member this week, as Jesus washed feet.
fathers: “Since he himself has declared and said of the bread, This is my Body, who shall dare to doubt any longer? … Do not regard the bread and wine as simple elements, for they are, according to the Lord’s declaration, the Body and Blood of Christ” (Mystagogical Catecheses 4, 1 and 6).

“It is not man who makes the gifts become the Body and Blood of Christ, but Christ himself, who was crucified for us. The priest stands there carrying out the action, but the power and grace are of God” (Homily on the Betrayal of Judas 1, 6).
magis: The Lord instituted the Eucharist at the Last Supper as the memorial of his death and Resurrection, the new Passover.
The Church draws her life from the Eucharist; it was born in the upper room.
The Eucharist is a sacrifice because it re-presents the sacrifice of the Cross.
saints: Friday 26 March: Good Friday (the collection is for the Holy Land). Saturday 27 March: Holy Saturday. Sunday 28 March: Qyomtho, the Resurrection.
2027-03-25.prayer: Lord Jesus, on the night you were betrayed you gave us your Body and Blood and washed your disciples' feet. Thank you for the Holy Qurbono and for the priesthood. Make us worthy to receive you, humble to serve one another, and faithful to stay with you in your agony. Amen.

quick: On this night Jesus gave us the Holy Qurbono.
He is the true Passover Lamb who saves us.
The One who gives his Body washes our feet: Eucharist and service.
2027-03-25.action: Spend time in adoration tonight, keeping Jesus company.
2027-03-25.question: How do I prepare to receive the Lord's Body and Blood?
2027-03-25.special: Pesaha (Maundy Thursday): Holy Qurbono of the Lord's Supper and the washing of the feet. In 2027 also the date of the Annunciation; follow the eparchy's direction.
illus: On Pesaha night St Thomas Christian families gather around the table, and the eldest breaks the Pesaha appam marked with a cross and shares it with everyone, even those away abroad who are remembered by name. The whole family becomes an upper room.

family.explain: On the night before he died, Jesus had a special meal with his friends. He took bread and said, “This is my body,” and the cup, “This is my blood.” That is how he gave us Holy Qurbono.
family.intention: We thank God for the Holy Qurbono and pray for our priests.
family.ask: Ask: “What can each of us do to serve someone in our family this week?”

kidsaint: The youngest apostle, who rested his head on Jesus' chest at the Last Supper and later stood at the foot of the Cross with Mary. Lesson: stay close to Jesus, especially when it is hard.
term: From the Hebrew for “Passover”. Maundy Thursday, when the Lord instituted the Holy Qurbono and washed the disciples' feet. Kerala Christian families break the Pesaha appam at home in the evening.
termMore: At the Pesaha service the bishop or priest washes the feet of twelve persons, as Jesus did (John 13:1–15), showing that the Eucharist leads to humble service.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, tonight we enter the upper room. Jesus says: “I have eagerly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.” He knew what was coming: betrayal, arrest, the Cross. And on that night he gave us his greatest gift.

“He took bread, gave thanks, broke it and gave it to them, saying: This is my body, which is given for you. Do this in remembrance of me.” And the cup: “This cup is the new covenant in my blood.” The lamb of the first Passover saved Israel from death; Jesus, the true Lamb, gives himself to save the whole world. Every Holy Qurbono since that night is this same gift.

And at the same table Jesus taught them how to be great: “I am among you as one who serves.” He knelt and washed their feet. We cannot receive the Body of Christ and refuse to serve the body of Christ in our brothers and sisters. The altar and the towel belong together.

Tonight, at home, families will break the Pesaha appam. Let it be a real family communion: forgive one another, remember those far away, thank God for the Qurbono and for our priests. And after supper, do not leave Jesus alone. Stay with him, as he goes out to pray in Gethsemane. Amen.
kids: Children, tonight is Pesaha. The night before Jesus died, he had a special supper with his friends. He took bread and said: “This is my body.” He took the cup and said: “This is my blood.” That was the first Holy Qurbono!
Then Jesus knelt down and washed his friends' feet, like a servant. He wanted to teach them to love and help one another.
Tonight at home, help someone without being asked. Let's say: “Thank you, Jesus, for giving us yourself!”

intro: Theme: “This is my body, given for you.”
On this holy night Jesus eats the Passover with his disciples, gives us the Holy Qurbono and the priesthood, and washes their feet. Everything we are as a Church flows from this Upper Room.

sub: In Egypt the blood of the lamb on the doorposts saved the people from death.
Jesus takes bread and the cup: his body given, his blood poured out, the new covenant.
He is the Lamb whose blood marks us in Baptism and feeds us in the Qurbono.
q: The blood shall be a sign for you on the houses where you live: when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and no plague shall destroy you.

Then he took a loaf of bread, and when he had given thanks, he broke it and gave it to them, saying, “This is my body, which is given for you. Do this in remembrance of me.” And he did the same with the cup after supper, saying, “This cup that is poured out for you is the new covenant in my blood.”
points.apply: Receive Holy Communion tonight with deep faith that it is truly the Lord.

sub: Isaiah foresaw a feast for all peoples on God's mountain.
St John hears: “Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb.”
Every Qurbono is a foretaste of that eternal banquet, and Jesus made his apostles priests to celebrate it.
q: On this mountain the LORD of hosts will make for all peoples a feast of rich food, a feast of well-aged wines.
And the angel said to me, “Write this: Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb.”
points.apply: Pray tonight for your priests, and for vocations to the priesthood.

sub: Abraham welcomed strangers: “Let a little water be brought, and wash your feet.”
Jesus, Lord and Teacher, kneels and washes his disciples' feet.
The Eucharist and service cannot be separated: whoever receives the Lord must serve the brethren.
q: Let a little water be brought, and wash your feet, and rest yourselves under the tree.
So if I, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet. For I have set you an example, that you also should do as I have done to you.
points.apply: Do one humble service at home tonight or tomorrow, especially for someone you find difficult.

concl: Jesus loved his own to the end. In the bread and the cup he gives himself; in the basin and towel he shows how to love.
Let us receive him with faith, adore him with gratitude, and serve one another with humility.
2027-03-25.resolve: Stay with the Lord in prayer for an hour tonight, as he asked his disciples.
